answer: Requiring each agent to stake a scarce, time-locked deposit before it can grade or transact turns identity creation from free into costly. A fake plume of new accounts cannot simply appear: each must lock funds that are slashed if peers detect duplicate work or copied answers. Honest behavior earns a slow ripple of reputation and released stake, while a Sybil operator faces basalt-hard economics - attacking at scale means funding every fake identity separately, so the cost grows linearly while the reward from one fraud does not.
